E-field analysis healthy tDCS

Diego Arias, PhD

2026-09-15

Stats analyses

1 - Avg. E-field magnitude

a) Linear mixed-effect model

mod1 <- lmer(avg_roi_E_magn ~
               #Fixed Effects
               FS*grp_age +
               #Random Effects
               (1|subID),
               #Define the data:
               data=sub_data_all.df, REML = TRUE)

summary(mod1)
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method [
## lmerModLmerTest]
## Formula: avg_roi_E_magn ~ FS * grp_age + (1 | subID)
##    Data: sub_data_all.df
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: -324.4
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -1.7033 -0.4753 -0.0546  0.4313  2.1358 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups   Name        Variance  Std.Dev.
##  subID    (Intercept) 5.316e-04 0.02306 
##  Residual             2.981e-05 0.00546 
## Number of obs: 62, groups:  subID, 31
## 
## Fixed effects:
##                  Estimate Std. Error        df t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)      0.137932   0.005923 30.580976  23.286   <2e-16 ***
## FSon            -0.005301   0.001930 29.000000  -2.746   0.0103 *  
## grp_ageYNG       0.008344   0.008515 30.580976   0.980   0.3348    
## FSon:grp_ageYNG  0.007197   0.002775 29.000000   2.593   0.0148 *  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##             (Intr) FSon   gr_YNG
## FSon        -0.163              
## grp_ageYNG  -0.696  0.113       
## FSn:grp_YNG  0.113 -0.696 -0.163

b) Stats report

report(mod1)
## We fitted a linear mixed model (estimated using REML and nloptwrap optimizer)
## to predict avg_roi_E_magn with FS and grp_age (formula: avg_roi_E_magn ~ FS *
## grp_age). The model included subID as random effect (formula: ~1 | subID). The
## model's total explanatory power is substantial (conditional R2 = 0.95) and the
## part related to the fixed effects alone (marginal R2) is of 0.07. The model's
## intercept, corresponding to FS = off and grp_age = OLD, is at 0.14 (95% CI
## [0.13, 0.15], t(56) = 23.29, p < .001). Within this model:
## 
##   - The effect of FS [on] is statistically significant and negative (beta =
## -5.30e-03, 95% CI [-9.17e-03, -1.43e-03], t(56) = -2.75, p = 0.008; Std. beta =
## -0.22, 95% CI [-0.38, -0.06])
##   - The effect of grp age [YNG] is statistically non-significant and positive
## (beta = 8.34e-03, 95% CI [-8.71e-03, 0.03], t(56) = 0.98, p = 0.331; Std. beta
## = 0.35, 95% CI [-0.36, 1.06])
##   - The effect of FS [on] × grp age [YNG] is statistically significant and
## positive (beta = 7.20e-03, 95% CI [1.64e-03, 0.01], t(56) = 2.59, p = 0.012;
## Std. beta = 0.30, 95% CI [0.07, 0.53])
## 
## Standardized parameters were obtained by fitting the model on a standardized
## version of the dataset. 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) and p-values were
## computed using a Wald t-distribution approximation.

c) Violin plot

##   - The effect of grp age [YNG] is statistically non-significant and negative
## (beta = -1.92e-03, 95% CI [-7.74e-03, 3.90e-03], t(56) = -0.66, p = 0.512; Std.
## beta = -0.24, 95% CI [-0.96, 0.48])
##   - The effect of FS [on] × grp age [YNG] is statistically non-significant and
## positive (beta = 6.56e-04, 95% CI [-2.72e-03, 4.04e-03], t(56) = 0.39, p =
## 0.699; Std. beta = 0.08, 95% CI [-0.34, 0.50])
## 
## Standardized parameters were obtained by fitting the model on a standardized
## version of the dataset. 95% Confidence Intervals (CIs) and p-values were
## computed using a Wald t-distribution approximation.
